title: Introduce cost synthesis engine + telemetry bridge for automated batch/cache/quant suggestions
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Motivation: Operational teams repeatedly ask for a turnkey way to convert live telemetry into actionable batching, cache, and quantization defaults that match their unit economics and latency SLOs. Ad-hoc heuristics leak money or regress quality; manual tuning is slow. This PR introduces a lightweight 'cost synthesis' engine that consumes cost/latency telemetry and produces suggested profiles for batching parameters, cache prefix policy, and quantization presets.

What this PR does: Implements a telemetry bridge that exports token-level and request-level cost signals (token_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, per-token-latency-estimate) into the optimizer pipeline, a cost synthesis core that (1) simulates tradeoffs using historical distributions and hardware models, (2) scores candidate profiles against user SLO/cost targets, and (3) emits a ranked set of suggested defaults. Adds an interactive CLI (econplay) to run local simulations with profile preview and an option to generate a JSON patch for Redwood defaults.

Key design points: 1) Non-invasive data flow: telemetry bridge subscribes to existing metrics streams (OTLP) and writes aggregated deltas to the optimizer queue; PII is never transferred. 2) Hardware-aware simulation: the synthesizer includes simple kernel/throughput models (FP16, INT8/4) for NVIDIA and AMD SKUs we support; these models are intentionally conservative. 3) Multi-objective scoring: cost, tail-latency (p99/p999), and quality delta (measured by eval hooks/provided prompt set) are combined with configurable weights. 4) Safe rollout: suggested profiles include a canary policy and automatic fallback to previous defaults if quality regression exceeds thresholds.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the synthesizer scoring, mocks for telemetry inputs, and integration tests that run econplay against a recorded workload (small corpus ~300 requests). Benchmarks run in perf-canary were used to validate that suggested profiles reduce per-token cost by median 18% on the recorded workload while keeping p99 latency within target for the canary config.

Backward compatibility: The synthesizer is opt-in; no change to runtime defaults happens until operators apply the generated JSON patch or enable auto-deploy in the Console. The telemetry bridge gracefully degrades when OTLP streams are missing.

Security and privacy: Telemetry bridge sends only aggregated numeric signals. We added an audit log entry for each synthesize run. The on-prem installer can disable telemetry bridge endpoints.

Docs and UX: Added docs/ops/cost-synthesis.md with conceptual docs, CLI examples, and a sample rollout policy. Console integration hooks are stubbed out (UI work tracked in ENG-4210).

Follow-ups: - Wire console acceptance flow and auditing (ENG-4210) - Expand hardware models with customer telemetry samples - Add further quality regressions metrics per-model

Detailed changes, commits and files changed are below. This description intentionally contains actionable details and rollout guidance so reviewers can focus on safety and model-eval concerns.
commits: feat(synth): add core cost synthesis engine and profile scorer
feat(telemetry): OTLP bridge writer and aggregation worker
feat(cli): add econplay simulator CLI with JSON patch export
test: add unit tests for scoring and simulation harness
perf: add canary workload replay and benchmark scripts
docs: add ops guide and rollout examples
fix: handle missing telemetry gracefully in bridge
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Nice end-to-end flow, thanks. A few safety questions: how do we ensure the quality evals are representative?

Priya Kapoor: Added eval hooks and a small prompt set in perf-canary; we also log per-profile sample outputs and diff statistics so reviewers can spot regressions. We discuss broader dataset curation in follow-ups.
Jian Li: The OTLP bridge looks fine but we should ensure backpressure doesn't blow up memory. Can we cap the aggregator queue?
Priya Kapoor: Added a bounded ring buffer and a backoff policy; pushed fix in 'fix: handle missing telemetry gracefully' commit.
Luca Martinez: Tests look reasonable. One request: add an explicit opt-in feature flag for auto-deploy in the Console API so customers don't get surprised.
Priya Kapoor: Added feature flag stub and documented the opt-in flow in docs; Console wiring tracked in ENG-4210.
Ethan Park: CI flaky test 'synth_scaling_test' was failing on first run (timeout). Increased test timeout and split into smaller assertions; CI passed on rerun.
Jian Li: Approved after nit fixes.
bot(mergify): all checks green; merging via squash.
release_notes: Add a new cost synthesis engine and telemetry bridge that generate recommended batching, caching, and quantization profiles from live telemetry. Opt-in; includes econplay CLI and rollout safety features. See docs/ops/cost-synthesis.md for details.
notes: Performance canary showed median ~18% per-token cost reduction on sample workload; individual tenants will vary. This PR is intentionally conservative with hardware models to avoid unsafe aggressive quantization recommendations.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 46 passed; Integration harness (replay): success; Perf canary: benchmark scripts executed, compare/plot outputs added under perf-canary/artifacts.
how_to_validate: 1) Run tools/econplay against perf-canary/workloads/small-replay.json. 2) Review suggested profiles in examples/suggested-profiles/sample_patch.json. 3) Apply sample patch to a non-prod Dedicated cluster and monitor quality metrics and cost delta via Console. 4) Confirm audit log entries appear in ops/audit.
